title: Approximating Irrational Numbers
seo_title: Grade 8 Approximating Irrational Numbers and Square Roots Worksheets (TEKS 8.2B, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.2B approximate the value of an irrational number, including π and square roots of numbers less than 225, and locate that rational number approximation on a number line
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.2B: perfect squares, estimating square roots and π, the nearest tenth and locating irrational numbers on a number line. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find the perfect squares on either side.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perfect squares: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225.
  • To estimate √n, find the perfect squares on either side: √50 is between √49 = 7 and √64 = 8.
  • 50 is very close to 49, so √50 ≈ 7.1.
  • π ≈ 3.14, so π is between 3 and 4.

Examples

Example

Estimate √30.

25 < 30 < 36

5 < √30 < 6

5.5² = 30.25

Answer: ≈ 5.5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Halving instead of taking the square root√36 = 6, not 18.
Picking the wrong perfect squaresList the squares near the number first.
Placing √n closer to the wrong number√50 is near 7 because 50 is near 49.

faq.a: Approximate the value of an irrational number, including π and square roots of numbers less than 225, and locate that rational number approximation on a number line.
225 = 15², so you only need the squares up to 15.

items.q: A square garden has an area of 64 square meters. How long is each side?

items.e: Side = √49 = 7 ft. Perimeter = 4 × 7 = 28 ft.

items.q: A cube has a volume of 27 m³. What is the area of one face?
items.e: Edge = ∛27 = 3 m. One face = 3 × 3 = 9 square meters.

items.q: A square photo has an area of 50 in². About how long is each side?

items.q: A cube has a volume of 64 ft³. What is its total surface area?
items.e: Edge = ∛64 = 4 ft. Each face is 16 ft², and a cube has 6 faces: 6 × 16 = 96 ft².

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Square root means the number that multiplies by itself: √81 = 9 because 9² = 81.

items.e: 7 = √49, and 50 > 49, so √50 is greater.

Why does x² = 36 have two solutions?
items.e: A positive and a negative number both square to 36: 6 and −6.

items.q: Why does x³ = −8 have a solution, but x² = −4 does not?
c: (−2)³ = −8, but no real number squared is negative
items.e: A negative times a negative times a negative is negative, but any square is 0 or more. (−2)³ = −8, but no real number squared is negative.

items.q: A square has a side of √20 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = (√20)² = 20 square centimeters.
